title: Magnify AR with a beaker: anodic alumina capacitors over logic
idea: On a $150k 28 nm MPW die, deposit aluminium in the BEOL and anodize it into self-ordered pores (about 65 nm pitch, AR above 100), then ALD-line them. Each cell's landing pad captures about 8 random pores, so no pore-to-transistor registration is needed. Demonstrate a 10 fF-per-cell capacitor-over-logic DRAM macro in a university cleanroom within 18 months.
why: Charge wall and capital: high-AR capacitors made electrochemically at room temperature, with no high-AR etcher. The prototype fits easily inside $1M.

title: Bamboo nodes: two-deck capacitor stitched at a conductive landing node
idea: Bamboo grows tall in segments joined at nodes: etch the capacitor hole as two ~45:1 decks with a TiN landing 'node' and SiN support ring between them, as 3D NAND does for two-deck channel holes, then form the electrode and dielectric continuously through both decks. The effective aspect ratio reaches ~90-110:1 without one extreme etch.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1, needs AR ~115): ~1.6-2x capacitor area, so Cs 8-10 fF or today's Cs at a smaller F.

title: Per-tier back-gate plane biased negative during retention
idea: Worse: let one worst-case leaky cell among billions set the refresh period. Flip: embed a thin conductive back-gate plane under each channel tier as part of the deposited stack and pump it negative during retention to suppress tail leakage, releasing it during access for full drive.
why: Pushing the <=13 fA tail toward ~1 fA could stretch refresh ~10x, cutting the 46 fJ/bit refresh energy and the 10-20% bandwidth tax (fact 3).

title: Deep-trench energy-reserve die flushes stacked DRAM to NV tier
idea: Capacitive energy storage as architecture: each memory stack includes one silicon deep-trench capacitor die holding enough energy (~mJ) to copy every DRAM tier into an on-stack ferroelectric or NAND tier over wide internal buses within ms of power loss. The stack keeps DRAM speed and gains non-volatility.
why: Meets non-volatility without a new cell, keeps DRAM performance, and removes server-level NVDIMM batteries; claim persistent memory for <5% added stack cost.

title: Lizard basking: per-tier refresh follows the stack's thermal gradient
idea: Lizards shuttle between sun and shade; in a 3D stack over logic, top tiers near the spreader run ~10-15 C cooler than bottom tiers, so embed a thermistor per tier group, refresh each tier at its own temperature-derived rate, and place refresh-sensitive or rarely touched data in the coolest tiers.
why: Uniform worst-case refresh at 125 C wastes ~2x on cooler tiers; tier-specific refresh recovers 30-50% of refresh energy and bandwidth at grade-1 temperatures.

title: Multi-fab tier sourcing: thin tier wafers from mature U.S. fabs
idea: Po: every tier comes from a different factory. Define an open 10 um-thin 'tier wafer' standard (array plus local sense, standard bond grid, redundancy lanes) that any 28-40 nm U.S. fab can make; a stacking house hybrid-bonds 8-32 known-good tiers from different suppliers onto a base logic die with per-tier remap.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: idle mature fab capacity produces DRAM bits; incremental capital is ~$50M stacking lines rather than $15B fabs.

title: CCD memory fixed: vertical bucket-brigade strings feeding one base sense amp
idea: 1970s CCD memory died because serial charge shifting made access slow. Keep its strength, no per-cell contact, but cap strings at 8 vertical tiers. Charge packets in gated wells along a vertical channel are clocked down into one sense amp at the base, the whole string is latched into SRAM in about 20 ns, and it is written back in reverse order. This removes per-tier staircase and bitline contacts.
why: Attacks the contact/staircase cost of 3D DRAM (fact 2). Because DRAM already overfetches 128x (fact 8), a serial burst costs little. Target is 8 bits per 4F2 pillar footprint.

title: Defense low-volume rule: one template for every tier, decoded vertically
idea: Defense users need many small memory variants and each imprint template is precious; make every tier identical, printed with one template, and select tiers not with a staircase but with a chain of tier-select transistors in each vertical bitline pillar, driven by a decoder in the bonded logic die. Products differ only in tier count.
why: Staircase area (~5-10% of die) and the KrF/ArF resist-trim steps that need krypton, argon and neon disappear; one template for all tiers (fact 4).

title: Sulfur-vapor conversion of patterned molybdenum gives per-tier MoS2 channels
idea: In each BEOL tier, sputter 1-2 nm Mo pre-patterned into channel islands and convert it to MoS2 in sulfur vapor at ~450 C (no H2S); the 0.65 nm channel keeps electrostatics ideal in a 20 nm lateral transistor and its 1.8 eV gap limits off-current.
why: An ultrathin, low-leakage, indium-free lateral transistor solves the 3D blocker (fact 2) at BEOL thermal budget; ~15 nm tiers instead of ~40 nm double tiers per stack height.

title: Rotate the crystal under the layout for quieter channels
idea: Zero added masks: rotate the 4F2 vertical-channel array 45 degrees relative to the wafer notch (or start from (110) wafers) so channel sidewalls become {100} planes, which have ~3x lower interface-trap density than {110}.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): the trap-assisted tail sets refresh, so fewer interface traps can shift the ~13 fA tail down and stretch refresh intervals for the price of a layout rotation.

title: Magnify cells per transistor: vertical CCD shift-register string
idea: Stack 8 storage nodes along one vertical channel and clock the tier gates as CCD phases, so charge packets shift down bucket-brigade style to a single access transistor and sense node at the bottom. This is 1970s planar CCD memory turned 3D.
why: Density and the access-transistor problem: 8 bits per access device and bitline contact, cutting 3D transistor count about 8x, with serial latency of about 20-40 ns.

title: MLCC-line ferroelectric block: one transistor, many plate-selected capacitors
idea: IFR: 'capacitor layers cost what a commodity chip capacitor costs.' Backward: use multilayer-ceramic-capacitor tape casting and screen printing to co-fire a block of thin doped-BaTiO3 layers where each layer is its own plate line, and bond an oxide-TFT glass lid giving one transistor per vertical column, a 1T-nC ferroelectric chain read by pulsing one plate at a time.
why: Capital (fact 4): runs on lines that make trillions of parts a year with near-zero new capex; low density (~10 Mb/mm2) and ferroelectric endurance must be proven.

title: Tier-multiplexed sense-amp layer shared by sixteen bonded array layers
idea: Limit: 0% periphery on any array die. Sixteen thin array layers are hybrid-bonded onto one bottom sense-amp layer. Each layer's bitline group reaches the sense amps through a per-layer select transistor in a vertical bond-via column, so one sense-amp row serves 16 layers in turn.
why: Fact 7: periphery is about 49% of the die; amortizing sense amps over 16 layers cuts periphery per bit about 16x and lifts array efficiency toward 90%.

title: GC-rich bonds: ultra-wide-bandgap Ga2O3 channels let capacitors shrink below 1 fF
idea: Thermophile genomes are GC-rich (three hydrogen bonds per pair) for a higher melting point; likewise use ALD Ga2O3 (Eg ~4.8 eV) as the vertical channel in each tier, whose thermally generated off-current stays ~1e-21 A even at 125 C, so a sub-1 fF planar MIM capacitor per tier holds data for seconds.
why: Capacitor wall plus 3D blocker at 125 C: removes the tall capacitor entirely, flat ~30 nm tiers make 100+ tier stacks feasible, and refresh drops ~1000x versus Si at 125 C.

title: Tunnel-FET access transistors in vertical 3D strings
idea: Po: the transistor opens only by quantum tunnelling. Make the vertical access device a heterojunction TFET (p+ SiGe source, intrinsic Si channel, n drain) with no thermionic subthreshold tail, giving aA-level off-current; its low on-current is acceptable because the 3D storage node is only ~1 fF.
why: Refresh eliminated by ~1e4x lower off-current than MOSFET tails; steep slope also lowers wordline voltage (fact 10).

title: Heterostructure hole-well pillar: capacitorless 4F2 vertical cell
idea: IFR: 'the transistor is its own capacitor.' Backward: grow the vertical channel pillar with a 5 nm Ge-rich SiGe quantum well mid-pillar; holes trapped behind the valence-band offset shift the threshold and are read non-destructively as drain current, written by band-to-band tunneling.
why: Charge wall and destructive read (facts 1, 8): no capacitor at 4F2, gain read, retention set by band offset rather than junction leakage.

title: Open tier-PDK and known-good-tier marketplace
idea: Limit: no single company may own the whole stack. Publish an open interface spec for bondable array tiers (pad pitch, test pads, select-switch protocol) so fabs of many sizes sell tested array tiers to independent stackers that assemble them on logic.
why: Capital intensity: splits a $15B monolithic fab into smaller tier fabs and stackers, so capacity scales in about $1-2B increments.

title: 2050 engineer's atom-thin tiers: 2D-semiconductor lateral access transistors
idea: From 2050, silicon tiers look too fat. Grow monolayer MoS2 or WSe2 by MOCVD at <=400C on each tier's dielectric to make the lateral access transistor, so a tier shrinks to ~15 nm versus ~60 nm for Si/SiGe.
why: The ~1.8-2 eV gap pushes the leakage tail well below 1 fA (Fact 3), and thin tiers allow 100+ tiers within today's etch depth (Fact 2).

title: Few-electron Coulomb-blockade nanodot strings along vertical pillars
idea: Coulomb blockade: a ring of ~2 nm Si nanodots in a thin tunnel oxide along each vertical channel pillar stores 3-10 electrons per bit. Charging energy quantizes the charge state and helps it resist leakage, while the thin barrier allows ~10 ns low-voltage writes. The layout follows 3D NAND, but the low fluence aims at high endurance.
why: Gives a non-volatile 3D cell at DRAM-like speed and lower voltage (facts 2 and 10); claim 3D NAND-class density with 1e10+ cycles, given the tiny charge moved.

title: E-paper bistability: antiferroelectric cell read nondestructively by capacitance
idea: Like e-paper holding an image unpowered, use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor with asymmetric electrodes whose built-in bias keeps it stable in either the AFE or field-induced FE phase, then read with a 50 mV AC probe of differential capacitance (the phases differ ~2x), disturbing neither state, so no restore and no refresh.
why: Destructive read and refresh (facts 3, 8): no full-swing restore, no refresh; claims >10x lower read energy (50 mV probe vs ~1 V restore).

title: Child's magnifying glass: green-laser crystallized silicon tiers over CMOS
idea: A child focuses sunlight to burn a spot without heating the whole table. Deposit a-Si at 350C on finished foundry CMOS, melt-crystallize it with a short-pulse 532 nm line laser so the transistors below stay cool, and build 2-4 tiers of top-gate poly-Si gain-cell TFTs.
why: Monolithic memory tiers over logic with a ~$1M laser and a PECVD tool (Fact 2, capital). Poly-Si leakage needs ms refresh, so it suits cache-like use.

title: Hairpin: U-turn vertical channel puts both cell terminals on top
idea: Bend the channel like a hairpin: etch a narrow slot in each 4F2 cell and line it with a U-shaped Si or oxide-semiconductor channel around a core gate, so source and drain both land on top and the bitline and capacitor contacts sit side by side above the cell. The channel is twice the slot depth long, which keeps leakage low, in a 4F2 footprint with no buried bitline.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) and 4F2 scaling (fact 4): ~100 nm effective channel in 4F2; claim a 10x lower leakage tail (4-8x longer refresh interval).

title: In/Ga-free ZnMgO:Al BEOL access transistors for stacked arrays
idea: Inverts 'oxide-TFT DRAM needs indium and gallium.' Use Mg-alloyed ZnO (band gap up to ~4 eV, Al-doped contacts) as the BEOL access channel and stack capacitor-cell tiers above the logic at <400 C.
why: Facts 2-3 and In/Ga chokepoints: the wide gap aims for leakage far below the 13 fA tail, stretching refresh toward seconds with abundant elements only.

title: Self-rolling Swiss-roll array: one patterned film becomes twenty tiers
idea: Worse: pay a full lithography and alignment cycle for every tier. Flip: pattern one long strained-bilayer (e.g., SiN on Si/SiGe or oxide-semiconductor) thin-film array once, then undercut a release layer so built-in strain rolls it into a tight multi-turn tube whose turns become tiers, with wordlines exiting at the tube ends and bitlines contacted along the outer seam.
why: Tier count is set by roll turns, not litho steps: ~20x footprint density from a single planar mask set; attacks EUV dependence and capital intensity (fact 4).

title: Breathing varactor capacitor stores at low voltage, reads boosted
idea: Po: the capacitor breathes. Replace the MIM capacitor with a MOS varactor whose plate line holds it in accumulation (high C) during idle so stored charge sits at ~0.2 V, then switches to depletion (C drops ~5x) at read to boost the node to ~1 V; at 0.2 V GIDL and junction leakage fall by orders of magnitude.
why: Refresh: idle leakage drive cut ~100x for tens of seconds retention, beyond working-set lifetimes; read gain also tolerates smaller Cs (fact 1).

title: Copper electroless bottom-up fill wires lateral wordline cavities
idea: After removing sacrificial SiN tiers through slits, line cavities with 2 nm ALD TiN, seed them with an aminosilane-anchored Cu nanoparticle catalyst, and fill by electroless Cu with a suppressor additive at the slit mouth so growth proceeds bottom-up and void-free.
why: Eliminates WF6 CVD and tungsten (China ~80%) from 3D wordlines and lowers wordline resistance ~3x, allowing longer wordlines with fewer driver and staircase regions (fact 7); runs on a wet bench.

title: Carbon wordlines: conformal nanographite replaces tungsten in replacement-gate cavities
idea: After the sacrificial nitride is pulled from each tier, fill the lateral wordline cavities with catalyst-free plasma-grown nanocrystalline graphite (C2H2, ~450 C) and intercalate it with FeCl3 to cut sheet resistance; no WF6, no fluorine attack on the gate oxide and no TiN barrier liner.
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and the 3-5 nm liner that eats tier thickness; ~15% thinner tiers per stack height and a W-free 3D DRAM bill of materials.

title: Chef's vinaigrette separation: block-copolymer hexagonal pillar masks
idea: Oil and vinegar separate on their own. Spin-coat high-chi PS-b-PDMS, anneal it into hexagonal cylinders at 16-24 nm pitch, and guide them with a coarse 248 nm pattern (graphoepitaxy). The result is transferred into a hard mask for a 4F2 vertical pillar array.
why: Sub-20 nm pillar patterning with a spin coater, hotplate and etcher. That is EUV-free and within a 10-person team's tool budget (Fact 4).

title: Block-copolymer cylinders multiply ArF guide patterns into pillar lattices
idea: [Box: MIM charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF-immersion guide trenches + PS-b-PMMA DSA, 4x density multiplication] Print coarse ~80 nm guide trenches with ArF immersion and let a block copolymer self-assemble into ~20 nm-pitch hexagonal cylinders inside them; the PMMA domains become the hard mask for VCT pillars and capacitor holes.
why: No EUV (fact 4): polymer thermodynamics multiplies density, replacing EUV on the 2-3 densest array layers at roughly a third of the litho cost per layer.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous-silicon donor wafers reused for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Canon's ELTRAN layer transfer (epitaxy on porous Si, split at the porous layer) lost to Smart Cut. It suits bonded 3D DRAM tiers well: grow each tier epitaxially on porous Si, bond, split, re-porosify the donor and repeat about 20 times.
why: Cuts crystal growth per tier ~20x, and with it demand for Spruce Pine quartz crucibles (a resource chokepoint), making many-tier bonded 3D DRAM affordable (fact 2). Donor wafers are recycled by design.

title: Radio broadcast reads: one activation multicast to many consumers
idea: One transmitter serves a whole city; in a 3D DRAM-on-logic stack, activate a row of shared weights once and multicast it over a base-die broadcast bus to all 16-64 compute tiles subscribed to that row address in the same step (batched or tensor-parallel inference).
why: Activation and movement energy (facts 5, 8): one access serves N consumers; claims 10-60x lower energy per delivered weight in batched inference.

title: Rotate the page vertical: one activation reads one cell per tier
idea: Use 3D geometry to shrink the page from an 8-KB row to a single vertical word: run the wordline as a vertical gate pillar through 64 tiers and give each tier its own short lateral bitline to a local sense amp. One activation touches exactly the 64 cells of one word.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): targets ~5.9 pJ falling to <0.5 pJ per useful bit, and large shared rows that invite row hammer disappear (fact 9).

title: Eliminate binary storage: three-level cells paired across adjacent tiers
idea: Store three charge levels per cell and pair cells vertically across two tiers so 9 states encode 3 bits in 2 cells; a shared vertical reference ladder in each pillar tracks temperature and leakage drift.
why: Density/cost per bit: +50% bits per cell pair with no extra lithography; needs ~2x sense margin, which short vertical bitlines provide.

title: Wordline breakers resize the activated row to each request
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: insert a tiny switch transistor every 64 columns along each local wordline (or at each mat of a 3D wordline plane). Column address bits decide how many segments connect, so a 64 B random request opens ~512 bits instead of an 8 KB page while streaming requests still open the full row.
why: Fact 8: activation energy per useful bit falls from ~5.9 pJ toward ~0.5-1 pJ for random access (5-10x), and fewer cells are disturbed (helps row hammer).

title: One CZ donor wafer supplies twenty tiers via repeated layer splitting
idea: Substitute 'one CZ wafer per device layer' with 'one CZ donor per ~20 layers': H/He co-implant a donor, bond to the growing stack, split at ~400 C, restore the donor with touch CMP and H2 anneal (no HF), re-implant; each transferred 50-200 nm single-crystal Si layer becomes a partially pre-processed array tier.
why: Quartz-crucible chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%): CZ wafers per bit fall 10-20x for stacked tiers; single-crystal tiers beat deposited channels on leakage tail.

title: Crystal-pulled nanowire forest as 4F2 vertical access transistors
idea: Borrow crystal growth: place SiGe seed nubs at 4F2 sites with spacer-defined dots and grow vertical single-crystal Si nanowires by self-catalysed selective epitaxy, then backfill gate-all-around wordlines and land capacitors on top, so the access transistor is grown rather than etched.
why: 4F2 vertical channels are ~33% smaller than 6F2 (fact 4), and etch-damage-free gate-all-around channels tighten the 13 fA leakage tail that forces refresh (fact 3); self-catalysed growth avoids gold contamination.

title: Nautilus septa: each tier group sealed in its own hermetic chamber
idea: The nautilus seals each shell chamber with a septum pierced only by the siphuncle; deposit hermetic ALD Al2O3/SiN septa above and below every few tiers of an oxide-semiconductor 3D array, pierced only by metal-plugged vertical bitlines, so moisture and hydrogen from upper layers cannot migrate down during 10 yrs at 125 C.
why: Hydrogen and moisture ingress is a key oxide-channel failure path at 125 C; compartmentalization confines damage and slows drift by orders of magnitude, complementing gettering.

title: Honeycomb anodic pores grow litho-free 300:1 capacitor arrays
idea: Like bees and corals that self-organize hexagonal cells, anodize a thick Al (or Ta) film over the access-transistor array so self-ordered hexagonal pores (25-40 nm pitch, AR >300:1) form spontaneously, registered to imprinted dimples over each storage contact; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN then lines the pores after field-assisted barrier-layer thinning opens the pore bottoms.
why: Capacitor charge wall and litho capital: AR 200-300 capacitors with no EUV and no high-AR plasma etch; ~2-3x Cs per footprint and 1-2 fewer EUV layers.

title: Coral reef: self-ordered anodic alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: Coral builds its skeleton bottom-up: deposit ~1.5 um of Al over the transistor array, pre-dimple it at each storage-node landing pad, and anodize it. Self-organized pores grow straight down from the dimples at aspect ratios beyond 100:1, and lining them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN makes the capacitors with no high-AR plasma etch.
why: Capacitor wall and capital (facts 1, 4): AR >100:1 from wet electrochemistry; claim capacitor-module capex -50% and Cs ~8 fF.

title: Laser-seeded single-grain channels erase the leakage tail
idea: Po: every transistor is carved from a perfect crystal. In each 3D tier, crystallize the access channel from amorphous Si by location-controlled excimer-laser growth from a seed hole (micro-Czochralski) so every channel is one grain; grain-boundary trap-assisted tunnelling, the main source of the fA tail in polycrystalline tiers, disappears.
why: Refresh: tail collapses toward the median (>10 s at 85 C) so refresh can be disabled for lifetime-bounded data; also tightens tier-to-tier Vt (fact 2).

title: Anodic alumina nanopores template 40-nm-pitch vertical transistors
idea: Let self-ordering electrochemistry pattern below the litho scale: anodize an aluminum film so hexagonally ordered pores form at ~40-60 nm pitch, set by the anodizing voltage. Coat the pores by atomic-layer epitaxy with gate dielectric and a semiconductor channel to make vertical surrounding-gate transistors; 180-nm litho only defines mat boundaries and straps.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4): 4F2-like density at an effective F of ~25 nm without any stepper below 180 nm.

title: RFID fluidic self-assembly: shaped DRAM tiles settle into logic sockets
idea: Five-cent RFID tags place millions of chips by letting shaped dies settle into matching wells in a liquid flow; dice DRAM arrays into 0.5 mm trapezoidal tiles, flow them over a logic wafer with matching recesses and hydrophilic capillary pads, then hybrid-bond in nitrogen. Logic wafers get stacked memory at wafer throughput with no pick-and-place and no argon plasma activation.
why: Die-to-wafer bonding throughput and cost (fact 6) improve ~10-100x, known-good tiles raise stack yield vs wafer-to-wafer, and memory directly over logic cuts data movement (fact 5).

title: Femtosecond-laser-written volumetric memory inside a glass block
idea: IFR: 'the array is written in the volume with no layers at all.' Backward: focus femtosecond pulses inside a doped glass block to precipitate conductive nanowire lines, laser-crystallized high-k capacitor voxels and oxide-semiconductor channel segments, writing word lines, bit lines and cells in 3D at ~0.5-1 um voxel pitch in one machine.
why: Capital (fact 4): a ~$1M laser writer instead of a fab; ~1e9 cells per mm3 if laser-formed devices switch reliably.

title: Copper wordlines and bitlines buried beneath the cell array
idea: Under 400 C, an oxide 4F2 vertical-channel array never heats buried wiring past 400 C, so buried word and bitlines can be damascene Cu, normally banned under a DRAM cell flow. Sub-array lines get about 2-3x longer per local driver.
why: Fact 7: fewer sub-wordline drivers and sense-amp stripes; about 10-15% die area goes back to cells.

title: Display fabs build IGZO memory tiers on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: [Box: 2T0C gain charge | IGZO TFT | current sense | many-tier panel-level stack | 2.2 x 2.5 m glass | i-line/ArF dry steppers in existing LCD/OLED fabs] Use idle display-fab capacity to build IGZO gain-cell arrays at ~0.5 um F on huge glass panels, stack 8-16 tiers, and dice them into CXL capacity-tier memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and supply: at 8F2, F=0.5 um gives ~60 GB/m2 per tier, ~340 GB per panel tier; glass costs ~100x less per m2 than processed Si, with no EUV.

title: Substrate-agnostic memory credit to convert existing non-silicon fabs
idea: IFR: 'new memory capacity appears in months, not 3-5 years.' Backward: extend the 48D advanced-manufacturing credit plus DoD/DOE guaranteed-offtake contracts to memory made on glass, foil or SiC substrates, and fund conversion kits (oxide ALD, panel steppers) for existing U.S. display, thin-film-PV and power-semiconductor lines.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital (fact 4): uses already-built non-silicon fabs; conversion at ~5-10% of a DRAM fab's cost per unit of capacity.

title: Minify the page to 64 bits with AND-gated wordline slices
idea: Split each wordline into 64-bit slices, each with a local AND gate that combines the row decode with a column-group select, so a random 64B access fires only 512 cells instead of 8 KB of cells.
why: 128x overfetch and the 5.9 pJ per useful bit of a random read: activation energy per useful bit could fall by 10-16x, and row-hammer disturbance is limited to the active slice.

title: Vertical capacitor column segmented per tier, lateral transistors
idea: Swap the usual 3D orientation: keep transistors lateral in each tier but etch one deep vertical capacitor trench per cell column through all tiers; each tier's storage-node layer is exposed as a ring on the trench wall (isolated from neighbors by the inter-tier dielectric), a scalloped recess enlarges it, then one conformal high-k and a common plate fill finish every tier's capacitor at once.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2): one HAR etch makes N tiers of ~0.7-1.5 fF capacitors without lateral capacitor recess; viable with short bitlines, aiming at break-even below 26 tiers.

title: Floating-plate differential capacitor shared by two stacked cells
idea: Worse: give each cell its own plate electrode, plate contacts and a single-ended half-signal. Flip: place one capacitor dielectric directly between a storage node in tier k and a storage node in tier k+1 so the two access transistors write complementary charge across it, storing one bit differentially with no plate line at all.
why: Doubles sense signal per fF so Cs can roughly halve (fact 1) and removes plate-line wiring and contacts from the 3D stack (fact 2).

title: Telephone line concentrators: one sense amp serves 1024 bitlines
idea: Adapted from telephone line concentrators where many subscribers share few trunks: a tree of oxide-TFT pass switches inside the array tiers lets 1,024 bitlines share one CMOS sense amp, and each cell is an active gain cell so it can drive the long shared path instead of sharing tiny charge.
why: Sense-amp and periphery area fall ~95% (fact 7), collapsing CMOS area per GB so arrays stack on a cheap base, ~100x cost cut with tier stacking; trade-off: ~1 us per full row, fine for bulk capacity.

title: Bookshelf memory: upright thin dies edge-bonded onto logic
idea: Limit: fixed footprint, no TSVs, and more than 32 dies. Stand 20 um thin DRAM dies on edge like books across the logic die, and hybrid-bond their polished edge pads directly to the logic surface. About 50 dies per mm of row.
why: Facts 5 and 6: far more dies per footprint than horizontal HBM stacks, a TSV-free signal path, and each die cools through its faces.

title: Print coarse, heat-shrink fine: shrink-film substrates compress cells sixfold
idea: Print the array at 2.5 um features on biaxially pre-strained polyolefin or polystyrene shrink film, then heat it so the web contracts ~60% linearly, compressing cells to ~1 um while rigid oxide films buckle into controlled wrinkles that add capacitor area.
why: Cheap printing resolution sets density; a 2.5x linear shrink gives ~6x more bits per m^2 without finer tools, and wrinkling adds plate area for free (fact 1); the risks are cracking and registration under shrink.

title: Eliminate TSV keep-out: vertical bus runs through scribe lines
idea: Stack whole memory wafers without singulating between dies in a column; place all vertical power and signal vias in the scribe streets that are otherwise wasted, so the active die area has zero TSV keep-out, and dice the finished stack once.
why: HBM TSV tax: removes TSV and keep-out area from the die (a large part of HBM's ~3x area/bit penalty) and avoids per-die thinning yield loss.

title: Ferrite flux-rod through the stack broadcasts data to all dies
idea: Revive the magnetic core threaded by many wires: one high-permeability ferrite-filled vertical via runs through a 16-die stack and each die's on-chip coil wraps it, so a transmit coil on the base die couples to every die at once like a shared core. Data moves inductively (broadcast writes, time-sliced reads), replacing most HBM data TSVs.
why: Fact 6: one flux rod replaces dozens of TSVs, cutting TSV keep-out area and the 20-30% TSV-related yield loss; HBM area per bit falls ~1.5x.

title: Crepe-paper electrodes: controlled buckling doubles capacitor area
idea: Like crepe paper or pleated filters gaining area through wrinkles, deposit the bottom electrode on a compliant sacrificial underlayer with compressive mismatch so it buckles into 20-40 nm-wavelength wrinkles before dielectric and top-electrode ALD on mature tools.
why: +1.5-2x area per footprint permits lower aspect ratio or trailing-node cells (fact 1) without new high-AR etchers.

title: Chimney: micro heat-pipe thermal vias let HBM stacks grow taller
idea: A chimney draws heat straight up: etch dummy 10 um vias through the core dies at hotspots, aligned through the stack to the lid, and fill them with sealed two-phase micro heat pipes or a Cu-diamond composite. Bottom dies run 10-15 C cooler, so 16-24-high stacks fit the thermal envelope without changing the HBM interface.
why: Layer count capped by heat: +50% dies per stack at the same footprint and interface, and cooler dies need less refresh (fact 3).

title: Selective SiGe oxidation converts sacrificial tiers into stacked buried oxides
idea: Substitute etch-and-fill tier isolation with in-place conversion: oxidize a Si/SiGe superlattice from its slit sidewalls at 750-850 C, where SiGe oxidizes 5-20x faster than Si, so each SiGe tier becomes buried insulator and the stack becomes multi-tier SOI; a thin Si:C barrier on each Si tier blocks rejected Ge from the channels.
why: Isolates stacked single-crystal channels (fact 2) without HF or fluorocarbon dielectric etch; fully depleted SOI body per tier tightens the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: Sliced laminate edge face exposes every bitline for side contact
idea: Laminate printed array foils, saw the block perpendicular to the bitlines and polish the cut face so every bitline of every foil appears as a dot at ~25 x 10 um pitch, then print redistribution or bond an edge-mounted silicon sense die directly onto that face.
why: Removes vertical vias entirely: a 10 cm x 2.5 mm edge face offers ~1M contacts, giving each bitline a direct sub-cm path to a silicon sense amp, so periphery (fact 7) lives off-foil on dense silicon while the foil stays pure array.

title: Sealed air-gap tiers to slash bitline capacitance
idea: Worse: pack dielectric between cells so bitline parasitics dwarf the cell capacitor. Flip: build tiers with sacrificial carbon or SiGe spacers between lateral cells and bitlines, then remove them through the slit and pinch-seal, leaving k~1 gaps around every bitline.
why: Signal scales with Cs/(Cs+Cbl): cutting Cbl ~40-50% lets Cs fall from ~5 fF to ~3 fF, shortening lateral capacitors and tiers (facts 1, 2) and reducing hammer coupling (fact 9).

title: Snap-through bistable buckled nanobeams in released tier cavities
idea: Euler buckling bistability: compressively stressed SiN/TiN nanobeams, released in cavities in each tier, rest bowed up or down. Electrostatic electrodes snap a beam between its two states without any contact, and capacitive sensing reads the position. Zero standby power, and no stiction or contact wear.
why: Gives non-volatile, leakage-free stacked bits with no refresh (fact 3) and no exotic materials; claim fJ-scale snap energy and high endurance because there is no contact.

title: Cross-die shared redundancy pool for stacked memory
idea: Combine stack interconnect with repair: rather than each die carrying its own spare rows and columns, pool spares on one die (or spread across the stack) and remap failing rows of any die through the base die's TSV/bond network with a content-addressable remap table.
why: HBM yield (fact 6, 20-30% loss): stack-level sparing rescues dies that fail per-die repair, raising stack yield ~10-15 points and trimming per-die spare area 2-3%.

title: Eliminate planar sense-amp stripes: tier-flipped checkerboard mats
idea: In a two-or-more-tier stack, place the sense-amp strip of tier N directly above the cell mat of tier N+1 and vice versa in a checkerboard, so no footprint is spent on SA stripes and bitlines stay short.
why: Periphery ~49%: SA stripes (~15-20% of planar die) vanish from the footprint, and short bitlines raise the Cs/Cb ratio.

title: Read floating-body state through the wordline's capacitance, not current
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: keep the bitlines quiet and sense the cell on the wordline instead. Stored body holes change gate-to-channel capacitance (accumulation vs depletion), so a small probe pulse on the vertical wordline couples a state-dependent charge into a wordline-side charge amplifier.
why: Fact 3 and 8: non-destructive, near-zero-current read with no hot-carrier disturb of capacitorless states; read energy ~5x lower.

title: Plate-less floating capacitor between complementary bitlines (2T1C)
idea: [Box: differential floating MIM | two lateral transistors | fully differential SA | lateral 3D tier | Si | ALD] Connect each end of a lateral 3D capacitor through its own access transistor to BL and BLB on opposite sides of the tier, with no common plate; data is the sign of the voltage across the capacitor, so a read gives twice the 1T1C signal from one capacitor and the plate layer disappears from every tier.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1) and tier height (fact 2): 2x signal halves the required Cs, and dropping the plate cuts tier stack height ~15-20%.

title: Plain-weave bitlines: true and complement swap metal levels every cell
idea: Like warp yarn passing over and under weft, route each bitline pair on two metal levels that cross at every cell pitch through a self-aligned via, so coupling from neighbouring bitlines and wordlines averages out continuously instead of in area-hungry twist regions; open-bitline 4F2 arrays gain folded-array noise immunity.
why: BL-BL coupling eats sense margin in 4F2 open arrays; continuous weaving recovers ~30-50% of signal so Cs can drop from ~5 fF toward ~3 fF (fact 1) or bitlines can double in length, halving sense-amp count (fact 7).

title: Multilateral oil wells: six lateral cells branch from one hole
idea: Borrowed from multilateral drilling, where one vertical well feeds many horizontal laterals: each vertical bitline hole in a 3D stack is recessed in six directions per tier by a crystallographic wet etch, forming six lateral cells in a star around one vertical line.
why: Vertical holes per bit fall ~3x vs two-sided designs, ~2x 3D bit density per footprint (fact 2).

title: Magnify old ideas: buy dormant trench-capacitor DRAM IP
idea: Acquire dormant legacy trench-capacitor DRAM patents and design data at distressed prices, then adapt the deep-trench array to a U.S. specialty foundry's existing deep-trench module for a niche legacy-DRAM product.
why: U.S. manufacturability: a DRAM path with no stacked-capacitor etch or EUV. The IP plus feasibility study fit under $1M.

title: Reverse-graded threshold tiers replace the 3D staircase
idea: Each tier gets two series n-type select transistors whose thresholds are graded in opposite directions across the stack (set by deposition recipe per tier, no mask). Driving pillar A to Vt_j+d and pillar B to Vt'_j+d leaves only tier j with both transistors conducting: a window decoder. The only added mask is the two select-pillar holes.
why: 3D cost and area (fact 2): replaces most of the staircase with ~16-20 voltage-decoded tiers per coarse group, cutting staircase masks and area by ~10x.

title: Grounded shield tiers interleaved so no row has a neighbor
idea: Po: no row has a neighbour. In a stacked 3D DRAM, insert a grounded doped-Si or metal shield tier between active tiers and route wordlines so laterally adjacent cells belong to rows separated by a grounded wall; deposition tiers are cheap, so spending one tier in three on shielding buys electrostatic isolation.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): aggressor-victim coupling cut >10x, raising the threshold from ~1k toward 100k activations and removing mitigation refresh traffic.

title: Eliminate on-die charge pumps: VPP delivered from package PMIC
idea: Remove VPP, VBB and VBLH charge pumps and regulators from every DRAM die; supply them from one high-efficiency package-level PMIC through dedicated backside power vias shared across the stack.
why: Periphery and energy: pumps are a meaningful slice of periphery area and run at 30-50% efficiency; external DC-DC at ~85% cuts wordline-supply energy ~2x.

title: Eliminate air breaks: never-break-vacuum linear cluster for tiers
idea: Deposit all channel, dielectric and electrode films for 32+ tiers in one linear vacuum cluster with in-situ remote-plasma hydrogen cleaning between steps, so there is never a native oxide and never a wet pre-clean.
why: Water: pre-deposition wet cleans are a large share of a fab's UPW; doing a whole tier stack in vacuum replaces dozens of rinses with one, per stack.

title: Williams-tube revival: field-emitter arrays write charge on bare film
idea: Adapted from the 1940s CRT Williams-tube memory and field-emission displays: a CMOS-driven field-emitter tip array (one tip per ~1,000 bits) sits ~1 um above an unpatterned dielectric storage film in vacuum; each tip deflects its micro-beam to deposit charge spots and reads them by secondary-emission current.
why: The storage film costs cents per wafer and needs no transistors, wires or litho; only the tip array is patterned at relaxed pitch, ~100x lower cost per bit in principle; trade-offs: vacuum package, 100 ns-1 us access, spot drift needing refresh.

title: Field-emitter-array Williams tube writing charge spots on blanket film
idea: Revive the Williams tube and GE's BEAMOS: a CMOS die carrying a Spindt-tip field-emitter array (one tip per 64x64 spot patch, electrostatically deflected) is vacuum-bonded a few microns above an unpatterned MOS/dielectric target, writing bits as ~30 nm charge spots and reading them by beam-induced current. The storage plane has no lithographic cell, capacitor or access transistor.
why: Facts 1, 2 and 4: the storage layer needs zero masks and zero EUV; if 30 nm spots hold charge, density rivals DRAM at a fraction of capital per bit with ~50 ns beam-settle access.

title: AND-gated cell activates only the addressed 64-bit segment
idea: Stack a column-gated vertical transistor in series with each cell's lateral access transistor so a cell reaches its bitline only when both its wordline and its column-select line are high; a random read then disturbs only the 64 addressed cells instead of the 8 kb row.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): activation energy scales with bitlines swung, so ~5.9 pJ per useful bit falls toward ~0.05 pJ; the extra device lives in Z, preserving 4F^2, and fewer opened cells also slows row hammer (fact 9).

title: Electrolytic-capacitor heritage: self-ordered anodic alumina capacitor mold
idea: Thirty-year industrial power supplies rely on anodized aluminum's self-ordered pores; e-beam-evaporate aluminum (no argon sputter) over the array, pre-indent it by imprint to lock the pore sites to the ~40 nm cell pitch, and anodize it so straight nanopores at AR 300+ form in an electrolyte bath. ALD TiN/high-k/TiN into the pores to make one capacitor per landing pad.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): AR 300 gives ~4x Cs or lets a lower-k dielectric work, using only wet anodization with no plasma etch or rare gas.

title: Project Ara lesson: optically coupled hot-swap memory tiles
idea: Google's Project Ara modular phone failed partly because its electro-permanent-magnet connectors could not carry enough bandwidth reliably. Couple swappable DRAM tiles to the host through short free-space optical links (VCSEL and photodiode arrays through a glass window), held by a mechanical latch. Tiles hot-swap with no wear-prone electrical connector.
why: Dense bandwidth with no contacts to wear (fact 5), plus field-replaceable, recyclable memory capacity.

title: MLCC-style nanolaminate storage capacitor with interdigitated ALD electrodes
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitors get high capacitance cheaply from hundreds of interleaved electrodes; build each DRAM storage node as an ALD nanolaminate of 6-10 alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers (nitrogen purge, no sputtering) in a lateral cavity, contacting odd electrodes on one side and even electrodes on the other by selective wet recess. Capacitance scales with layer count instead of aspect ratio.
why: Capacitor wall (fact 1): ~3-5x Cs per footprint without AR 115 or k 70, sized for lateral 3D DRAM tiers (fact 2).

title: Running-bond brick stacking: each chiplet straddles two below
idea: Lay DRAM chiplets like bricks in running bond: each upper die is offset by half a die and hybrid-bonded to two lower dies, so vertical links form a 3D mesh with two paths to every die instead of a single TSV column.
why: One bad TSV column kills an HBM stack today (fact 6: 20-30% yield loss); path diversity tolerates failed links and spreads heat; claimed +15-20 points of stack yield.

title: Accordion-folded die strip: one thinned strip folded into sixteen tiers
idea: Map-folding origami: fabricate a long strip of 16 array segments on one wafer, thin to ~10 um, replace the silicon between segments with polyimide hinges carrying the bus wiring, then Z-fold the strip into a stack held by die-attach film, so every tier is electrically continuous without TSVs or tier-to-tier alignment.
why: Removes the HBM TSV tax (fact 6: ~3x wafer area per bit, 20-30% yield loss) and bond-alignment failures; claimed ~2x bits per wafer area versus HBM with stack yield set by per-segment repair.

title: Wavelength-addressed photoconductive wordlines through vertical light pipes
idea: Photoconductivity: SiN waveguides thread vertically through the 3D stack, and each tier taps them with a micro-ring drop filter tuned to that tier's wavelength. The dropped light switches photoconductive a-Si/IGZO access channels in place of gate metal. Choosing a wavelength picks the tier, and choosing a waveguide picks the row.
why: Removes the tungsten wordline metal (W chokepoint), the staircase and the high-voltage wordline drivers (facts 2, 7 and 10); claim tier count no longer limited by staircase area.

title: Self-locking p-type cell with ground-idled bitlines
idea: Po: the stored bit locks its own door. Use a p-type oxide access transistor whose back-gate is the storage node itself, on an insulating substrate, and idle all bitlines at 0 V: a stored 0 sees no drain-source bias so it cannot leak, and a stored 1 raises its own back-gate and drives the channel deeper off.
why: Refresh: both states are self-protected by removing leakage drive instead of fighting the tail; retention limited by dielectric leakage (hours).

title: Langmuir-Blodgett perovskite nanosheets as a k~200 room-temperature capacitor dielectric
idea: Work at the molecular scale with a 1930s Langmuir trough: float exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 perovskite nanosheets and transfer 5-10 monolayers onto storage electrodes at room temperature. That gives k~200 in ~10-nm films with no high-temperature anneal.
why: The capacitor charge wall needs k~70 (fact 1); k~200 cuts the required AR ~3x and suits low-temperature stacking of 3D tiers.

title: Stamped capacitors: nanoimprinted pillar forest on glass panels
idea: IFR: 'capacitors are stamped like coins, not etched.' Backward: UV-nanoimprint a hexagonal forest of 20:1 resin pillars onto a glass panel from a reusable master, ALD-coat them with electrode/high-k/electrode, optionally burn out the resin core for a double-sided shell, and build oxide TFTs above.
why: Litho and etch capital, charge wall (facts 1, 4): one stamp replaces EUV litho plus a 60:1 dry etch; masters are reused ~10,000 times.

title: Duplex printing: DRAM arrays on both faces of one wafer
idea: Adapted from duplex printing and logic backside power delivery: build the array on the front, bond to a carrier, thin, and build a second array on the backside of the same silicon, sharing periphery through nano-TSVs in the middle.
why: Roughly doubles bits per wafer start while sharing substrate and periphery, ~1.6x lower cost per bit.

title: Nano vacuum-channel triodes as zero-leakage access switches in BEOL tiers
idea: Bring back the vacuum tube at 20 nm: each 3D cell's access device is a vertical field-emission triode etched into dielectric (metal tip, gate ring, storage-node anode), needing no crystalline channel and leaking essentially nothing when off. Cells stack in 50+ BEOL tiers because no epitaxy or high-temperature anneal is required.
why: Facts 2 and 3: removes the single-crystal lateral transistor blocker for 3D and the <=13 fA leakage tail, stretching retention from 64 ms to minutes and cutting refresh energy (16-33% of idle) by >90%.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access devices with literal vacuum gaps
idea: Po: the switch is a drawbridge that lifts away. Replace each tier's access transistor with a lateral NEM relay (5 nm-gap Ru cantilever pulled in by the wordline) so the off state is a physical gap with no subthreshold or junction leakage; retention is set only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours to days).
why: Refresh eliminated; abrupt switching at ~0.5 V pull-in also attacks the voltage floor (fact 10). Risk: contact endurance must reach >1e15 cycles versus ~1e10-1e11 shown.

title: Counter-phase wordline drive on adjacent tiers cancels coupling
idea: In stacked 3D DRAM, whenever a tier's selected wordline ramps up, drive an unselected wordline segment in each neighboring tier down by a matched step (deeper off-state), so vertical capacitive kicks into the neighbors' bitlines and storage nodes cancel instead of accumulating.
why: Inter-tier disturb and row hammer (facts 2,9): 2-4x less vertical coupling lets tier pitch shrink (more tiers per um of stack) and lowers disturb-driven refresh.

title: Cheapest-bit market: convert idle 3D NAND lines to vertical-string DRAM
idea: Design for the buyer of the cheapest possible bits (the $50 laptop market): 3D NAND fabs already run 200+ tier staircase, channel-hole and replacement-gate tools on DUV only, so retool idle NAND lines to build vertical-string DRAM at relaxed F~40 nm with 64 tiers. License a cell that keeps the NAND tool set and swaps only the channel and storage modules.
why: Capital intensity and EUV dependence (fact 4): reuses $10B+ of installed tools, no EUV, and capacity in ~1-2 years instead of 3-5.

title: NbO2 Mott-selector over BEOL capacitor for 4F2 cross-point DRAM
idea: Mott insulator-metal transition: a doped NbO2 threshold-switch film is stacked directly on a BEOL MIM capacitor at each wordline/bitline crossing. Only the fully selected cell exceeds the ~1 V Mott threshold and charges; half-selected cells stay insulating. This gives a transistor-free 1S1C cell that can be repeated in 4-8 BEOL tiers over CMOS periphery.
why: Gives 4F2 per tier with no crystalline access transistor (facts 2 and 4); claim 4-8x bits per wafer area. The risk is off-state leakage, which needs a doping-engineered Mott gap.

title: $1-IoT block-copolymer pillar arrays guided by UV-LED exposure
idea: A $1 IoT memory needs dense pillars at near-zero patterning cost; spin a cylinder-forming block copolymer that self-assembles into a hexagonal ~22 nm pitch lattice of vertical-channel transistor sites, registered by coarse 200 nm guide posts printed with a 365 nm UV-LED stepper instead of a mercury-xenon lamp or excimer laser. Hexagonal packing gives slightly better than 4F2 density.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4) without EUV or rare-gas light sources; 4F2-class pillar arrays at <10% of EUV patterning cost.

title: Coaxial hole: capacitor sheath below, gate-all-around transistor above
idea: One high-AR hole per 4F2 site does both jobs: the lower ~80% is lined as a cylinder capacitor (plate/high-k/storage shell), and the top ~20% passes through a deposited wordline plane where a channel-all-around transistor joins the storage shell to a top bitline. Gate length is set by wordline-plane thickness, so capacitor and transistor share one etch and one alignment.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 4F2 (about 33% less area than 6F2) with full-height capacitor and no storage-node contact or landing pad, deleting ~2 critical litho layers.

title: Draw-tower lithography: fiber-drawn coaxial capacitor faceplates
idea: IFR: 'features shrink without a scanner.' Backward: build a centimeter-scale glass preform of low-melting-metal/dielectric/metal coaxial rods, draw it ~1,000x on a fiber tower, bundle and redraw to ~50-100 nm coax, and slice the fused bundle into 20 um plates, each a dense array of 200:1 coaxial capacitors to bond onto a transistor layer.
why: Charge wall and EUV (facts 1, 4): high-AR capacitors with zero etch or litho; the draw ratio replaces optical reduction.

title: Paper-stack tiers laminated with z-axis anisotropic conductive film
idea: IFR: 'stacking tiers is as easy as stacking paper.' Backward: build each memory tier on a reusable glass carrier over a laser-release layer, peel it off as a 5 um polyimide film, and laminate dozens of films with anisotropic conductive film whose particle chains conduct only vertically through aligned pads.
why: 3D tiers and HBM tax (facts 2, 6): known-good films are tested before lamination; no TSVs or hybrid-bond tools, and carriers are reused.

title: Gecko-setae dry adhesion: test whole stacks before permanent bonding
idea: Temporarily join stacked DRAM dies with gecko-like nanopillar dry-adhesive arrays plus spring micro-pillar contacts for electrical continuity, run full at-speed stack test, swap any bad die, then convert to a permanent bond with a low-temperature Cu-Cu anneal.
why: HBM yield tax (20-30% loss): known-good-stack rework stops one bad die scrapping 8-16 good ones, cutting lost stack value ~2-3x.

title: Layer-transferred InAs/AlSb resonant-tunneling floating-gate tiers
idea: Resonant tunneling: a triple-barrier InAs/AlSb stack passes charge into a floating gate only when ~2.5 V aligns the resonance, and blocks it otherwise, giving very long retention. The III-V layers are grown on cheap substrates, then oxide-bonded as 4 stacked tiers onto CMOS logic.
why: Gives low-voltage, high-endurance non-volatile working memory in 3D (facts 2 and 10); claim sub-fJ writes and >1e7-1e12 endurance, density multiplied by tier count.

title: Cu-Mn self-forming barriers replace TaN in array and bond metal
idea: Inverts 'copper wiring needs a Ta/TaN barrier.' Deposit a Cu-Mn alloy seed so Mn diffuses to the dielectric interface and forms a ~1-2 nm MnSixOy barrier on anneal, used for array bitlines, hybrid-bond pads and stack vias alike.
why: Ta (and Co liner) chokepoints removed; the thinner barrier leaves more Cu cross-section for ~20-30% lower line resistance at 20 nm.
